workbook_title: FOUNTAINHEAD Workbook Module 4: Internal & External False Beliefs

concepts.name: Module 4 Scope
concepts.definition: Module 4 of the FOUNTAINHEAD Perfect Webinar workbook focuses on Internal & External False Beliefs. It walks participants through Secret #2 (breaking internal false beliefs), Secret #3 (breaking external false beliefs), Making the Transition (asking permission to reveal the offer), and Preparing the Stack Slides.

concepts.name: Module 4 Agenda
concepts.definition: Session #1: Crafting Secret #2 (Overview of Perfect Webinar, Addressing Internal False Belief, Demonstrating the Framework, Workshop). Session #2: Crafting Secret #3 (Identifying External False Beliefs, Telling the New External-Belief Story, Showing the Framework to Support the New Belief, Workshop, Breakout). Session #3: Making the Transition (Asking Permission to Reveal Your Offer, Workshop). Session #4: Preparing Your Stack Slides (Workshop, Breakout). Next Week: What We'll Cover + Prework for Module #5.

concepts.name: Perfect Webinar Framework Structure
concepts.definition: A whiteboard map: (1) Map Origin Story & New Opportunity â†’ (2) Big Domino: The ONE Thing â†’ (3) Secret #1 Vehicle, Secret #2 Internal Belief, Secret #3 External Belief â†’ (4) Break and Rebuild Their Belief Patterns â†’ (5) Let Me Ask You a Question (Stack/Close). The entire arc is designed to convince the audience your framework is the best way to achieve their desired result (via the Big Domino) and knock down every key secret, story, and framework so they have no other logical or emotional option but to purchase.

concepts.name: Internal False Belief (Secret #2)
concepts.definition: Internal false beliefs are the doubts your audience has about their own ability to succeed with your framework. Secret #2 is designed to address and overcome these doubts. You discover the internal false belief by finishing the statement: 'I believe in your framework, but I don't think I can succeed because of [insert personal doubt].'

concepts.name: Demonstrating the Framework
concepts.definition: Your audience needs to see a clear, actionable path that proves they can achieve success with your framework. This is where you introduce a framework or case study that directly addresses their internal doubts. Most often done via a Demo or Case Study â€” show a real-world example of someone like them who has succeeded using your framework.

concepts.name: The 45-Minute Mark

concepts.name: External False Belief (Secret #3)
concepts.definition: External false beliefs are the doubts about external circumstances or challenges your audience blames for their lack of success. They are perceived obstacles that feel outside their control. Your goal in Secret #3 is to replace their false belief with a new empowering one. This new belief should open the door to success by showing them the obstacle is surmountable.

concepts.name: You Just Got Slapped... By Google
concepts.definition: A visual framing for the external-belief story: the audience has been 'slapped' by some outside force (Google algorithm, platform change, market shift). The new-belief story proves someone navigated that exact slap and came out ahead.

concepts.name: External Belief Framework Template (Traffic Example)
concepts.definition: A four-step framework that replaces the external false belief 'I can't drive traffic to my website': (1) Identify Your Competitors â€” find out who your competitors are, (2) Analyze Their Traffic Sources â€” use tools to see where your competitors are getting their traffic, (3) Target the Same Sites â€” buy ads on the same websites where your competitors are advertising, (4) Drive Traffic to Your Funnel â€” direct the traffic from these ads to your own funnel.

concepts.name: The Transition (Joe Bauer Method)
concepts.definition: A powerful technique, first introduced by Joe Bauer, that helps eliminate the awkwardness and makes the transition from teaching to selling feel natural and respectful. It is built on asking the audience for permission to reveal the offer, so they never feel ambushed.

concepts.name: The 8-Step Transition Sequence
concepts.definition: (1) Acknowledge the Value Provided â€” recap key points and reinforce value. (2) Ask for Permission â€” ask if they're open to hearing how they can take this further with your help. (3) Introduce the Offer â€” introduce the offer as a natural extension of the value. (4) Recap What You've Taught â€” 'We've covered [list].' (5) Engage the Audience â€” ask if they believe they could implement what they've learned. (6) Acknowledge Potential Overwhelm â€” recognize that implementing everything might feel overwhelming. (7) Ask for Permission â€” 'Would it be okay if I spent a few minutes showing you a way to make this easier?' (8) Pause for Response â€” wait for the audience to respond; this pause builds anticipation and respect for their input.

concepts.name: Why Permission Matters
concepts.definition: When you're delivering a presentation, the shift from teaching valuable content to offering a product or service can feel awkward. This session guides you on how to make this transition smoothly, ensuring your audience feels comfortable and receptive rather than caught off guard.

concepts.name: Transition Slide Architecture (Slides 52-55)

concepts.name: The Stack Slide Purpose
concepts.definition: Stack slides are essential for building up to your final offer in a persuasive, structured way. By the end of this session, you will have all the stack slides ready, setting the stage for the next module where we dive into the stack and the close.

concepts.name: The Full Stack Slide
concepts.definition: The master template â€” 'What You're Gonna Get...' â€” listing every product in the stack (Core Product In The Stack, 2nd through 5th Product In The Stack) each with its own dollar value, and a Total Value at the bottom. This is the base slide from which every intermediate stack slide is derived.

concepts.name: Progressive Stack Build
concepts.definition: The stack is revealed one layer at a time. Save a copy of the full stack slide, then create progressively revealing versions: First Stack Slide (only the core product), Second Stack Slide (core + 2nd), and so on through the Final Stack Slide which restores all components.

exercises.prompt: Save the Full Stack Slide â€” start by saving a copy of the full stack slide, which includes all components and the total value.

concepts.name: First Stack Slide Build
concepts.definition: Delete everything except for the first bullet point and its value. Calculation Required: ensure the total value reflects only the first component.

concepts.name: Second Stack Slide Build
concepts.definition: Save another copy of the full stack slide. Keep the first and second bullet points. Update the total value to include the sum of both components.

concepts.name: Repeat the Process
concepts.definition: Continue this process for each additional component of your offer. Each slide should include the next component in the sequence, with an updated total value.

concepts.name: Final Stack Slide
concepts.definition: The last slide should reflect the entire offer with all components and the final total value â€” effectively restoring the Full Stack Slide template as the climactic reveal.
